Opioids have no demonstrated benefit in primary headache disorders and carry a high risk of medication-overuse headache, sedation, falls and dependence in the older population in which hypnic headache typically presents. Bedtime caffeine, lithium or indometacin are the established options.

{{RuleMedication}} is used for other primary headache disorders, but evidence in {{RuleCondition}} is limited. Hypnic headache usually starts after age 50, where the anticholinergic burden, daytime sedation, orthostatic hypotension and falls risk of a tricyclic are significant. Start low, review early, and check for QT-prolonging co-medication.
